claims.text: The company presented 36-week Phase 2 liver-biopsy and lipid data for its lead liver-disease drug at a hepatology-conference plenary session on 12 Nov 2018.
The trial's week-12 primary-endpoint result (liver fat reduction by MRI-PDFF, p<0.0001) was already public in company disclosures by 13 Mar 2018.
36-week results -- NASH resolution 27% vs 6.5% placebo (p=0.02) and a >2-point NAFLD Activity Score improvement in 56% vs 32% of patients (p=0.02) -- were first announced 31 May 2018.
Cash and investments were $488.5 million at 30 Sep 2018, up from $191.5 million at 31 Dec 2017.
Total revenue was $0 for both the three- and nine-month periods ended 30 Sep 2018.

Management said it expected to begin a Phase 3 study in the primary liver-disease indication in late 2018 or early 2019, subject to regulatory approval, and said it was evaluating the design of a possible Phase 3 study in the related cholesterol-disorder indication that could begin in 2019.
Management said it believed it had significant financial resources to fund its currently planned Phase 3 programs.

In June 2018 the company completed an underwritten public offering of common stock, issuing 983,607 new company shares (plus shares sold by selling stockholders), with net proceeds to the company of about $282.8 million for general corporate purposes including R&D and clinical-trial costs.
Common shares outstanding rose from 14,227,634 at 31 Dec 2017 to 15,393,309 at 30 Sep 2018.
Net cash (cash and investments of $488.538 million minus total liabilities of $6.642 million) was about $481.9 million at 30 Sep 2018.

At the nine-month 2018 average quarterly cash-outflow rate from operations (about $6.41 million/quarter), the reported cash and investments balance would cover roughly 19 years before financing or spending patterns change -- a scenario, not a company forecast, and one that ignores the funding needs of the newly planned Phase 3 programs.

The company described the proposed pivotal-trial design for the primary indication as pending regulatory agreement, and did not disclose a completed regulator agreement on trial design as of the cutoff.

The trial (NCT02912260) enrolled 125 patients in a randomized (2:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled, multi-center design across about 25 U.S. sites; 73 drug-treated and 34 placebo patients had paired baseline/week-36 biopsies.
At week 12, liver fat was reduced 36.3% in drug-treated patients overall (42.0% in a pre-specified high-exposure subgroup) versus 9.6% for placebo (p<0.0001).
The liver-fat reduction was sustained at week 36: 37% for drug-treated patients versus 8.9% for placebo (p<0.0001).

Among drug-treated patients who achieved NASH resolution on biopsy, fibrosis also resolved in 50% of cases; overall, at least a one-point fibrosis reduction occurred in 29% of drug-treated versus 23% of placebo patients.
Significantly more drug-treated than placebo patients had normalization of a liver enzyme (ALT) associated with liver injury.
Adverse events were mostly mild to moderate and balanced between drug and placebo arms; mild loose stools were reported at the start of treatment in the drug-treated group.

In a separate, previously completed 116-patient Phase 2 trial in the related inherited high-cholesterol disorder, the drug produced an 18.8% placebo-corrected reduction in LDL cholesterol (p<0.0001), and 21% in patients on an optimal dose.
The company said it was evaluating the design and objectives of a possible Phase 3 study in the cholesterol-disorder indication that could begin in 2019.

No debt-related financial-statement line item (e.g., notes payable, long-term debt) appears in the structured (XBRL) data for fiscal 2017 or the first three quarters of 2018, and no interest expense was reported for those periods; the small liabilities balance ($6.6 million at 30 Sep 2018) appears to be short-term operating liabilities.
